subject: Historical fast-opening anchor + render-gap finding
summary: Slot01 found physical-test anchor 1.3.21 e754d77d: inner animation was THE SMOOTHEST VERSION YET. 1.3.21 opening used Samsung native panel handoff with no explicit inner shell wake; WakeInner entered in 1.3.24 and moved to DeviceState edge in 1.3.29. Current Gen4 clean DeviceState-triggered cycles show wake shellLatency=166 ms but topology reaches INNER_HANDOFF before Binder wake returns. Early cover visual starts immediately but is revoked while phase=CAPTURING, creating a measured bridge gap before first inner frozen frame.

historicalBuild.fieldResult: INNER SCREEN ANIMATION WAS THE SMOOTHEST VERSION YET

interpretation: Do not equate wake Binder return with useful readiness. In both clean early-edge cycles, Samsung publishes inner active/default topology 21.7-53.1 ms before wake returns. The visual bridge is dropped 67.6-83.2 ms before INNER_HANDOFF and 141.5-172.9 ms before first logged inner frozen frame. This render/ownership gap is a plausible contributor to perceived slow opening and is independent of slot02 SurfaceFlinger latency decomposition.
recommendedAB: Opening-only A/B: preserve current close/Gen4 authority, suppress explicit WakeInner while retaining DeviceState edge/render arming, and separately keep the cover bridge alive until confirmed inner useful presentation. Measure edge->inner topology and edge->first useful pixels for each factor independently.
